# Boundary theory and independent validation

Read `REPORT.md` for the Chinese findings and limitations. `PROTOCOL.md` records the main prospective design; `crossing_design_and_source_lock.json` records the later new-pool confirmation. The production DBGPS2 core is unchanged at f7b1373ec68bc6518af91b7427eda53699a3c73d.

## What was completed

- 330 main validation graphs, 7,920 parameter points, five frozen decision policies.
- 36 additional graphs from new 4,096-design pools, 864 parameter points, following the adjacent-downcrossing bound derivation.
- 24 parameter points on full unmerged raw HT176 reads, with all 16 first-phase overlapping points reproduced.
- Seven representative synthetic inputs independently regenerated byte-identically.
- Frozen native-search checks, reference-permutation invariance, independent candidate scoring, origin-count diagnostics, exact probability calculations, and false-output donor tracing.

Graphs and parameter points are not independent experimental replicates. Conditions have three independent design families; matched models and nested library sizes share designs. The new-pool confirmation is prospective relative to the downcrossing derivation, which itself occurred after seeing the original dependence-ignoring prediction fail. No new speed or full-file recovery experiment was performed.

## Main files

`policy_results.csv` and `crossing_policy_results.csv` contain all five policies on their respective graph cohorts. `native_grid_results.csv` and `crossing_native_grid_results.csv` contain every underlying c/r point. The real library appears only in the main files. The original 330-graph validation remains separately recorded rather than silently relabelled as a 366-graph preregistration.

`theory_bounds_validation.csv` retains the initial marginal/union analysis. `crossing_bounds_validation.csv` contains the sharper bound using adjacent downcrossings, including the new confirmation. Horizontal ranges in Figure 14 are model probability bounds, not confidence intervals. Simultaneous binomial intervals test compatibility with the model; neither intersection nor a narrow range establishes calibration on real DNA.

`runs/` and `crossing_runs/` contain per-input settings, input hashes, exact commands, grid summaries, truth-independent candidate/status bytes, native outcomes, and compact reference-assisted diagnostics. `*.blind_meta.json` gives candidate-array dimensions. Candidates are uint8 packed DNA, 41 bytes per codeword; ordering is r outer and c inner, with the lists in the saved command. Accepted status is 0. Rejected candidates are zero-filled and must be masked by status.

`clean_counts/` contains origin-correct window counts from Poisson-sampled inputs, as little-endian uint16 arrays of shape n by (201−k), at every genomic window start. Native `*.truth.u16` and `*.alts.u16` use their `*.oracle.json` dimensions. These arrays serve different purposes: native canonical counts can include matching words from other origins. References are for evaluation only and never guide traversal or the frozen policies.

`false_accept_forensics.csv` reports all erroneous native accepted outputs in the main grid, including three real-library points that are not selected by the reported policies. `false_candidate_donor_traces.csv` groups distinct simulated false candidates and records long exact matches in other designs. The new confirmation grid had no false accepted native outputs. Candidate agreement across correlated parameter settings is not proof of correctness.

`src/`, `bin/`, and all source-lock JSONs preserve the measured code. The binary is macOS arm64. `reference_evaluation_only/HT176_ref.fa` supplies the real scoring reference. The multi-gigabyte raw FASTQ files are excluded; paths, sizes and checksums are retained. No public accession for these local HT176 files has been verified.

The crossing-run text log has a cosmetic seed-label error: its print statement shows the final outer-loop seed, 23023, for every job. The locked job list, generated reference filenames, per-input settings, commands and measured outputs use the correct seeds 21021, 22022 and 23023. The original measured script is preserved unchanged; quantitative analysis uses saved per-job settings, never that log label.

## Reanalysis

With Python 3, NumPy, pandas and Matplotlib installed, run from the extracted folder:

```sh
python3 analyze_deep.py
python3 trace_false_candidates.py
python3 analyze_crossing.py
python3 make_figures.py
python3 write_report.py
```

These commands analyze saved measurements and do not execute the macOS binary or require raw FASTQ. Analysis resolves the saved synthetic and real evaluation references locally. Keep all measurement source/binary files intact so checksum checks remain meaningful. Figure rendering can differ with installed fonts and Matplotlib; regenerated figures need new visual inspection.

## New measurements and manuscript authoring

Preserve the original archive. Use a new output copy and new provenance files for measurement changes or another platform; the runners resume existing per-graph JSON records and validate their source locks. Configure external raw/historical paths before real-data reruns. The main and confirmation sources are different frozen stages; do not edit them and retain their original hashes as if they were newly measured.

The original profiler is included for provenance. The only new search-wrapper behavior records accepted native bytes before truth scoring. To build on a compatible system:

```sh
cc -O3 -Isrc -o bin/blind_profile src/blind_profile.c src/dbgps_codec.c src/dbgps_redundancy.c src/dbgps_strand.c src/kthread.c -lz -lpthread
```

The smoke workflow additionally uses the parent binary. The accompanying first-phase archive can be extracted as sibling `reconstruction_boundary/` to supply it. Run the smoke checks before a new measurement. Do not substitute new executable hashes into the historical execution locks.

The manuscript was updated from the prior serial/three-worker version, preserving all old media and equations. The revision changes title, abstract, Introduction, coverage interpretation, Results, Discussion, Methods, Code availability, Figures 14–16 and Table 8. Six editable OMML equations were added. Author/protocol/accession placeholders inherited from the source are still unresolved and are not invented here. Manuscript rendering uses the bundled document runtime; the authoring script's historical source/helper paths must be configured when reproducing it outside the workspace. The archived source manuscript and helper are included for that purpose.

No commits, pushes or external publication were performed. The source ZIP excludes raw FASTQ, scratch inputs, development smoke outputs, render QA PNG/PDF files, and Python caches. Scientific figure PNG/PDF/SVG files are included.
